decisions.question: topology-ir@v1's consumers frontmatter is [nidana.runtime, nidana.tooling, nidana.integration], while root D10 (S27) added nidana.navigation and nidana.flutter as consumers. Add them now, or wait for those nodes' confirm entries?

options.label: wait for their confirm entries
options.consequence: the frontmatter stays two consumers short until the navigation and flutter plans are reconciled; the registry's consumer count reads 3 meanwhile; no reconcile writes a consumer no plan emitted

options.label: add the two node ids now
options.consequence: the frontmatter matches root D10 at once, but reconcile writes a consumers entry that no pending section carries, outside step 4's rule

decisions.why: hsdd-reconcile step 4 applies confirm entries only, and S27's notes already route the two consumers through the navigation and flutter plans' confirm entries. phase_ids stays provisional either way, so nothing depends on the count before then.

decisions.question: The three confirm entries carry 'for consumer plans' sub-bullets (which producing phase delivers which guarantees, which phase a consumer's edge waits on). Consumer planners never read the producer's plan, and the registry projects no produced_by. Where does that schedule land, and what happens to each contract's 'Code owner: nidana.model, whose first phase lands every declaration below', which now misreads as nidana.model.1?

options.label: frontmatter only
options.consequence: produced_by lists six phases for topology-ir@v1 with no hint which one delivers the analyses; consumer planners either wait on the last producing phase (nidana.runtime on nidana.model.14 instead of .12) or guess; the stale 'first phase' text stays

options.label: a Delivery paragraph in each contract
options.consequence: each contract names the phase that lands its declarations, the phase a consumer's edge waits on and the phase that delivers each guarantee group, read from the plan's entries and gates; hsdd-config injects it with the body; reconcile must rewrite it if nidana.model is re-planned

options.label: the schedule in conventions.md
options.consequence: planners read it first, but one node's delivery schedule would sit in a tree-wide file, and hsdd-config would not carry it into consuming phase contexts

decisions.chosen: a Delivery paragraph in each contract
decisions.why: HSDD makes contracts the only inter-node knowledge (conventions, Parallel development protocol), so information addressed to consumer plans has to sit in the contract. The 'Code owner' clause now reads 'first producing phase' and points at the paragraph; topology-ir@v1's two Validation sentences that named nidana.model's first phase (expectMatchesSchema, consumers' stand-ins) now name nidana.model.2 and the Delivery paragraph. Guarantee lists come from the plan's --guarantee gates. The signal that would have changed my mind: a registry or hsdd-config feature that projects per-phase delivery from the producer's plan.
evidence: hsdd/spec/nidana.model.md (Phase Plan gates; confirm sub-bullets as drained)
.agents/skills/hsdd-contract/SKILL.md (Core principle: the body is injected into a consuming phase's context)

decisions.question: amend topology-dsl@v1 (stages, sinks, builders and plans compare by identity) was 'proposed as a new guarantee after G29, or as a sentence under The plan'. Which, and how is it covered per ADR-001 item 3?

options.label: G30 plus a sentence under The plan, with one recording case
options.consequence: a consumer (the live interpreter) can rely on it by id; the producer's recording replay checks it, identityHashCode included; one more case in recording_conformance.dart

options.label: a sentence under The plan only
options.consequence: no guarantee id, so no fixture is needed, but nothing checks it and a later value-equality override would pass every gate

decisions.chosen: G30 plus a sentence under The plan, with one recording case
decisions.why: The plan names a consumer that relies on it (an interpreter keying a map by stage, Live interpretation items 2 and 3), so it is a guarantee. The case is small: two reads of one topic, one handle written twice, two planOf calls; it passes against the existing stand-in and four seeded value-equality defects (stage, sink, builder, plan) each fail it alone. Compatible: no declaration changes and every existing case still passes. Version stays v1 with a Versioning line.

decisions.question: amend topology-ir@v1 (finding and collision constructors sort their lists into the Interface's orders): a new guarantee, or a change to G7's equality text? And is it compatible?

options.label: G23 plus a sentence under Analyses, with one behavior case
options.consequence: the orders become invariants of every value with an id consumers can cite; one more case in topology_ir_conformance.dart that sorting stand-ins pass and order-keeping ones fail

options.label: widen G7
options.consequence: no new id, but G7's existing cases would have to grow and the change would read as an edit of an existing guarantee

options.label: constructors keep the order given (the plan's named alternative)
options.consequence: no contract change; a hand-built finding equals an analysis's only when its author sorted it

decisions.chosen: G23 plus a sentence under Analyses, with one behavior case
decisions.why: The plan settled the sorting (nidana.model.10) and judged it compatible; the experiment confirms it: the full suite passes against a sorting stand-in, the old order-keeping stand-in fails only G23, and each constructor reverted alone fails only G23. No other contract's fixtures construct a finding or a collision, and bus-api@v1 G20 and nidana-checks@v1 read analyses' results, already in these orders. A new id keeps G7 unchanged, which the contract's Versioning lists as compatible ('a new guarantee that existing fixtures still pass'). The signal that would favor keeping the order given: a consumer that needs a finding to carry a caller's order; none exists.
evidence: grep of hsdd/contract/fixture/ for finding constructors

decisions.question: nidana.model's plan restricts its gates by --guarantee lists written before G30 and G23 existed: nidana.model.9's topology-dsl list and nidana.model.10 to .13's topology-ir lists omit them, so they first run at the unrestricted replays of nidana.model.11 and nidana.model.14. Edit the plan's gates here?

options.label: leave the plan; report it
options.consequence: G30 is first checked at nidana.model.11, G23 at nidana.model.14, one or four phases after their code lands; no gate fails

options.label: edit the gates
options.consequence: earlier checks, but reconcile edits a plan only to apply a collision's outcome (step 3), and the gates are hsdd-phase-plan's

decisions.why: hsdd-reconcile updates a plan only for a collision's losing side; the gate lists are hsdd-phase-plan's. Nothing breaks: the unrestricted replays run both cases. Listed for the orchestrator.

decisions.question: note 1 (root pubspec.yaml workspace list and pubspec.lock shared by every member-creating phase; proposed: list in path order, one member per line): does it change a convention, and where does it land?

options.label: conventions, Execution protocol
options.consequence: a 'Shared workspace files' bullet: path order, one line per member, cross-node changes reach the root one at a time, the lockfile re-resolved with fvm dart pub get and never hand-merged; every planner and executor reads it

options.label: an ADR-002 amendment through hsdd-adr
options.consequence: the list's form sits beside item 1's content rule, but a merge-discipline rule lands in a layout ADR and waits for a scheduled step

options.label: drop it
options.consequence: Collides with cannot name another node's phases, so the cross-node contention on these two files is recorded nowhere

decisions.why: It governs how phases on different lineages merge, which is the Execution protocol's subject (Textual contention serializes); ADR-002 item 1 stays the source of what the files contain. I added the lockfile rule the note implies: pub get --enforce-lockfile in every gate fails on a stale lockfile (exit 65), so a hand-merged lockfile is never acceptable. The signal for the ADR route: an ADR-002 amendment scheduled for other reasons.

decisions.question: note 2 (the replay tool's sets land in nidana.model.1, .2, .6 and .7, which adds non-contract waits for other nodes' gates): does it change a convention?

options.label: conventions, Phase design
options.consequence: a bullet beside the replay rule lists where each set lands and makes a phase that runs a set, or imports fixture.dart, depend on that phase; it tells readers to read ADR-001's, root D10's and the contracts' 'first phase' wording through it

options.label: only an ADR-001 item 9 amendment
options.consequence: the canonical home, but the next consumer plan (nidana.runtime, producer-first order) could run before the hsdd-adr step and would read 'written in its first phase'

options.label: drop it as derived data
options.consequence: no registry projects it, so consumer planners, who never read nidana.model's plan, would miss the behavior-set wait on nidana.model.6 and the file and cli wait on nidana.model.7

decisions.why: These are dependency edges no contract carries, and hsdd-phase-plan reads conventions first. A consumer waiting on nidana.model.5 does not reach nidana.model.6 transitively, so the behavior-set edge has to be stated. ADR-001 item 9 still needs its wording aligned (listed as an hsdd-adr step); the conventions line carries the facts until then.

decisions.question: note 3 (the conventions' 'Phase 1 of a leaf-parent is the type-level skeleton' holds for nidana.model only as a band; proposed text 'the type-level band, which opens the plan after any gate infrastructure an ADR places first'): apply, and how much?

options.label: rewrite the fp-progression paragraph
options.consequence: the band opens the plan after ADR-placed gate infrastructure, each contract's declarations land in its first producing phase (ADR-001 item 10), and 'the producer's first phase' in root D10, the Development flow, an ADR or a contract reads as the phase the contract's Delivery paragraph names

options.label: keep the old sentence
options.consequence: the conventions contradict an accepted plan (nidana.model D1, accepted by the orchestrator at S28) and every later planner reads 'phase 1' literally

decisions.why: The sentence is a convention and the accepted plan departs from it with a stated reason (D1, S28 orchestrator decision 'Accept the deviation'). The proposed wording is kept and extended with the reading rule, so root D10's and ADR-001's 'first phase' need no edit before their owners next touch them. A topology-dsl@v1 consumer waiting on nidana.model.5 rather than .4 is named as the shared-library case.

decisions.question: Should the Delivery paragraph this pass wrote become a convention for every later reconcile, so the steps that drain nidana.runtime's and the other plans do the same?

options.label: state it under Contracts
options.consequence: every later reconcile writes a Delivery paragraph when it drains a producer's confirms, and rewrites it on a re-plan; contracts stay uniform

options.label: leave it to each reconcile
options.consequence: later passes, run by other agents, may or may not repeat it, and consumers of different producers would find the schedule in some contracts only

decisions.why: A practice that only one contract family follows is worse than none: consumers would not know whether a missing paragraph means 'first phase delivers everything' or 'not written'. The conventions are where every reconcile looks first (hsdd-reconcile step 1).

decisions.question: note 4 (the replay tool's command semantics: exit codes 0, 1, 2 and 64, PENDING for every fixture naming an absent package, --set never adds a set, --guarantee with no id for a slug runs none of its behavior, file or cli cases, a bare G{n} belongs to the one slug named): does it change a convention?

options.label: no conventions change; an hsdd-adr step
options.consequence: the semantics stay in nidana.model D2 until an hsdd-adr step clarifies ADR-001 item 9; every node's gates see only pass or fail meanwhile

options.label: copy the semantics into conventions
options.consequence: a second home for tool behavior ADR-001 owns, which drifts when the ADR is clarified

decisions.chosen: no conventions change; an hsdd-adr step
decisions.why: The note is about the tool's behavior, which ADR-001 item 9 owns, not about a convention; the step prompt also bars an ADR edit here. Other nodes' gates depend only on exit status 0 versus non-zero, which ADR-001 item 9 already states, so nothing waits on the clarification.
